newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei plunges over 500 points in afternoon.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei plunges over 500 points in afternoon.

text.p: Tokyo stocks took another steep dive on Thursday, buckling under the weight of heavy losses in the banking sector as well as sporadic rounds of selling in futures contracts.
The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares fell by more than 500 points, or more than 2.6 percent, in afternoon trading.
The Nikkei slid as low as 18,177.98 points before clawing back up to 18,227.19. It was down by 453.74 points or 2.43 percent with half an hour left before the close.
The slide was the latest in a series of steep stock market descents fuelled by fears about the health of the Japanese economy.

Brokers said that bank shares were hurt by moves by cash-strapped Japanese firms to sell some of their bank and brokerage shareholdings ahead of financial year-end book closings at the end of March, brokers said.
Sakura Bank Ltd sunk to a limit-low, losing 100 yen to close at 699 yen. It was the second most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.
